title: Director of Product Management

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: This role bridges technical product capabilities with market demands and customer feedback at Drytac. With active presence at ISA Sign Expo and PRINTING United (demonstrated booth participation in 2024-2025), the Director of Product Management is directly exposed to customer pain points around outdoor durability failures, UV degradation complaints, and graffiti vandalism issues that plague current 5-7 year PVC films. They own go-to-market strategy for existing product lines (Weathershield, Polar Grip Air vehicle wraps, anti-graffiti films) and would personally benefit from a premium overlaminate solution that: (1) commands higher margins in their product mix, (2) reduces customer service escalations related to premature graphic failures, (3) enables positioning against lower-cost commodity competitors, and (4) supports their distributor network with a truly differentiated offering. This role's KPIs likely include revenue per product line, customer satisfaction scores, and competitive win rates - all directly improved by offering Tedlar's superior 12-20+ year performance as either a co-branded solution or white-label integration into their existing Weathershield portfolio.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: The Director of Product Management owns go-to-market execution for Drytac's existing product lines including Weathershield overlaminates, Polar Grip Air vehicle wraps, and anti-graffiti films. They likely report to the VP of Product Development and manage product marketing, pricing strategy, and voice-of-customer intelligence. This role sits at the intersection of technical R&D and commercial sales, translating market feedback from distributors and end-users into product roadmap priorities. They influence product portfolio decisions, competitive positioning, and new product launch strategies, making them a critical gatekeeper for evaluating external material partnerships or technology integrations.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Given Drytac's current portfolio, the Director would care most about use cases where Tedlar's 12-20+ year outdoor performance creates competitive separation: (1) Premium architectural graphics and building wraps where clients demand maximum lifecycle and are willing to pay for it—expanding beyond Weathershield's 5-7 year ceiling; (2) Fleet graphics and vehicle wraps (Polar Grip Air line extension) where fleet managers calculate total cost of ownership over 10+ year vehicle lifecycles; (3) Transit interiors and outdoor advertising where graffiti resistance reduces maintenance callbacks that strain customer relationships; (4) High-end signage projects where Drytac's distributors need a technical differentiator against commodity PVC competitors flooding the market. Each use case addresses their dual mandate: grow revenue through premium product tiers while reducing post-sale support issues.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: This role likely owns product line revenue targets, gross margin percentages, customer satisfaction/NPS scores, and competitive win rates in key segments. They personally care about solving: (1) Margin erosion as PVC films commoditize—Tedlar enables premium pricing; (2) Customer service escalations from UV degradation or graffiti damage on Weathershield products deployed in harsh outdoor environments; (3) Distributor feedback requesting longer-warranty options to compete in architectural and transportation segments; (4) Lost deals to competitors offering superior outdoor performance claims. Tedlar's 12-20+ year track record, graffiti resistance, and -70°F to 230°F operating range directly address these pain points while supporting their recent Pinnacle Award momentum by positioning Drytac as the innovation leader, not just another PVC supplier.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Drytac exhibited at ISA Sign Expo 2025 (April 23-25) and PRINTING United Expo 2025 (October 22-24), meaning the Director is currently synthesizing customer feedback and competitive intelligence from those events. Their recent PRINTING United Pinnacle Product Award for Interlam Eco Anti-Graffiti demonstrates active innovation in protective film categories. This post-trade show window (May-June 2025) is ideal timing as they evaluate product roadmap priorities for 2026 launches, assess gaps revealed at ISA/PRINTING United, and make decisions about expanding beyond their current 5-7 year durability ceiling before the next trade show cycle begins.

personalization_hooks.hook: Drytac's Weathershield series delivers 5-7 year outdoor performance, while architectural graphics and premium vehicle wrap segments increasingly demand 10+ year warranties
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Open by acknowledging Drytac's strong position in mid-tier durability, then frame Tedlar as enabling a premium tier expansion—addressing the performance gap the Director likely hears about from distributors serving high-end projects. Position this as portfolio evolution, not product replacement.

personalization_hooks.hook: Recent ISA Sign Expo and PRINTING United presence puts Director in direct contact with customer pain points around UV degradation and graffiti damage on current PVC-based films
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Reference post-trade show timing and ask about emerging customer requirements they observed at ISA/PRINTING United. Frame Tedlar as solving specific pain points their booth conversations likely surfaced—graffiti resistance for transit applications, extreme temperature performance for architectural wraps.

personalization_hooks.hook: Pinnacle Award for anti-graffiti innovation positions Drytac as a technology leader, not a commodity supplier
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Congratulate their Pinnacle Award and position Tedlar as extending that innovation leadership into the premium outdoor graphics segment. Emphasize competitive differentiation against Asian PVC imports where Drytac needs technical superiority to justify premium pricing and protect distributor margins.

recommended_approach: Lead with portfolio expansion opportunity rather than product replacement. Frame Tedlar as enabling Drytac to capture premium architectural and fleet graphics segments currently beyond Weathershield's 5-7 year capability, leveraging their recent innovation award momentum and post-trade show product planning window.
